app.title: LabBridge
app.summary: A person loads a plate-reader export, or a bundled sample. The interface detects the file layout and shows the raw table. Next they review a proposed mapping of each raw column to a standard schema, where every column has a confidence score and a colour (auto, needs review, unmapped), and they confirm or change each one. Quality checks then run, and the person sees a plate heatmap with flagged wells marked next to a table that gives each flag a severity and a reason. A validation step fits a standard curve, back-calculates sample concentrations, scores replicate agreement and charts positive-control history against Westgard limits, and ends in a pass, review or fail verdict. Finally the person checks every normalized value before and after, and downloads the clean dataset, a quality summary and the transformation log.

task.text: Turn a messy instrument export into a standardized, quality-flagged dataset and decide whether it is fit for analysis.

data.text: A long-format plate-reader export with one reading per well (well role, sample, analyte, value, unit, replicate, expected concentration), plus a history of control readings across runs and a log of every change and flag.

stage.text: cleaning and validating raw plate-reader exports before downstream analysis

mechanism.text: A six-step wizard with a progress stepper moves from upload to export, and each step needs the one before it: the checks run only once the column mapping is confirmed. The QC step shows a plate heatmap with flag markers beside a flag table sorted by severity. The validation step uses tabs for the curve fit, replicate CV bars, a Levey-Jennings control chart and a verdict banner.

field.text: plate-reader assay quality control with standard curves and Westgard rules

workflow.name: turn a raw instrument export into a validated, quality-checked dataset

steps.here: Drop a CSV or Excel export, or click Load sample plate export. The interface detects long or grid layout and shows the raw table with row and column counts.

steps.step: match raw columns to a standard schema, confirming the uncertain ones
steps.here: Each raw column gets a proposed canonical field, a confidence badge and a reason (exact, synonym, fuzzy or content match). A dropdown per column lets the person confirm or change it, and Confirm mapping & run quality checks runs the pipeline.

steps.step: flag problems in each item, with a reason
steps.here: Metrics show rows in and out, number of flags, errors, warnings and whether the data is ML-ready. A plate heatmap on a log colour scale marks flagged wells with triangles, beside a table of flags sorted by severity, each with its well, rule and reason.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Tabs fit a linear standard curve (R², slope, acceptance) and back-calculate sample concentrations with 95% CIs. They also chart replicate CV per sample against a fail line and plot positive-control runs against mean ±2/3 SD limits, with Westgard violations marked.

steps.step: decide whether the data is fit for use
steps.here: A PASS, REVIEW or FAIL banner, with one reason line each for the curve, replicates, outliers and control drift.

A before → after table of every normalized value (unit conversion, decimal comma, embedded unit, date, well coordinate, control spelling), with a toggle to show all of them, then the full clean table with a per-row qc_flag column.
Download buttons for the clean dataset (CSV), the data-quality summary (Markdown) and the transformation log (JSON). The summary renders inline and the log appears as a table.

distinctive: Column-to-schema mapping is explainable: each proposal carries a confidence score and the signal that produced it. Low-confidence matches wait for a human decision, and contested targets are resolved automatically.
Wells sit on a fixed 8×12 plate layout, so flagged readings are shown where they are on the plate, not just listed.
Control readings are tracked across past runs on a Levey-Jennings chart with Westgard rules (1_3s, 2_2s, shift), which catches reagent drift that checks on a single run miss.
Outliers are found with a robust median/MAD z-score, and replicate agreement is judged by coefficient of variation within each sample.
Nothing changes silently: every normalization and flag is written to an audit log that is exported with the data.
